It calls UploadToContainer and DownloadFromContainer on dockertest's own client, in integration/integrationutil/util.go. These calls send a plain tar buffer to whatever Docker daemon the test host runs. They are not the daemon code, and they are not part of the headscale server's attack surface. golang.org_x_net__CVE-2026-33814.reasoning:
CVE-2026-33814 (GO-2026-4918) is an HTTP/2 client-side infinite loop. The transport loops writing CONTINUATION frames after it receives a SETTINGS frame with SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0. It affects golang.org/x/net/http2 before v0.53.0 and the stdlib net/http before go1.25.10 (and go1.26.0 to before 1.26.3).

Presence: go.mod pins golang.org/x/net v0.32.0, which is below 0.53.0. The build toolchain is Go 1.23 (go.mod 'go 1.23.1', flake.nix buildGo123Module, Dockerfile.integration golang:1.23), which is below 1.25.10, so the stdlib net/http is in the affected range.

Reachability: the x/net http2 package is used only for the server side (http2.Server in hscontrol/noise.go). The advisory's x/net symbols are all client Transport symbols, and a search found no first-party use of them. The stdlib surface is reachable, though. hscontrol/derp/derp.go calls http.Client.Do, a listed vulnerable symbol, in loadDERPMapFromURL. It fetches each URL in derp.urls, whose default in config-example.yaml is https://controlplane.tailscale.com/derpmap/default. Over HTTPS, net/http negotiates HTTP/2 by default, and I found no setting that disables it. The response comes from a remote server, so a malicious, compromised or MITM'd endpoint could send the bad SETTINGS frame and hang that fetch goroutine.

Conditions: the HTTP/2 client is on by default, the URL fetch is on by default, and I found no mitigation in the repository. Impact is limited to denial of service, and the attacker must control or intercept the DERP map endpoint. The exact toolchain used for release builds is not pinned beyond Go 1.23, which is the main caveat.
